evals.name: helper-placement
evals.prompt: In my Next.js app, InvoiceTable needs a function that formats a row's due date as 'in 3 days' / 'overdue'. Nothing else uses it yet. Where should I put it? Add it.
evals.expected_output: Places the function next to InvoiceTable (same file or a sibling helpers.ts in its folder), named without a use prefix, pure and unit-testable; does not create or extend a global utils/ file; mentions promoting it only when a second consumer appears.
assertions: The function is not placed in src/utils or another global folder
The function name does not start with 'use'
The answer explains colocation / promotion on reuse

evals.name: cross-feature-import-review
evals.prompt: Review this change: src/features/billing/components/InvoiceHeader.tsx now does `import { useCurrentUser } from '@/features/auth/hooks/use-current-user'`. Anything wrong with the structure?
evals.expected_output: Flags the cross-feature import (struct-no-cross-feature) and proposes either composing both features at the route or moving useCurrentUser into the shared layer; suggests enforcing it with an import-restriction lint rule.
assertions: Identifies the feature-to-feature import as a violation
Offers composition at the route or promotion to shared as the fix
Mentions a lint rule (no-restricted-paths, boundaries or dependency-cruiser)

evals.name: business-logic-extraction
evals.prompt: This component has a 40-line reduce that computes a risk score and a verdict from findings, plus a useEffect that copies the filtered findings into state. Refactor it so the logic lives in the right place.
evals.expected_output: Moves score/verdict rules into pure framework-free functions (feature lib or helpers.ts) with unit tests, removes the effect+state and derives the filtered list during render, and keeps the component rendering only.
assertions: Business rules end up in plain functions without React imports
The useEffect that syncs derived data into state is removed
Filtered findings are computed during render

evals.name: barrel-file-request
evals.prompt: Create src/components/index.ts that re-exports all our shared components so we can import them from '@/components'.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on an aggregating barrel in app code (module-graph cost, cycles), recommends direct imports per component, and notes a one-line per-component index.ts is a separate, acceptable convention; does not silently create the aggregate barrel.
assertions: Explains the cost of aggregating barrel files
Does not create an export * barrel without flagging the trade-off

evals.name: negative-trigger
evals.prompt: Why does my useEffect run twice in development?
evals.expected_output: The skill should not be needed; this is a React behaviour question (Strict Mode), not code organization.
assertions: The frontend-ui-architecture skill is not the primary source of the answer
